chapter: Stuff Smith stories, Wes Montgomery and singers
title: The tune "Orson": the Ellington record and Jones playing it
summary: Jones recalls Ellington's early recording of Orson, playing it at Dante's with John Collins, and surprising Nat Adderley with it.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Did you ever run into Orson Welles anywhere else? In your music career?
No. No. The only other time I ran into him was the tune, "Orson."
Which was written for him, too.
Yeah.
And recorded by you, on "Ellington Is Forever"
Yeah.
Beautifully.
Thank you. The Ellington Orchestra had a great record on it too, at one time.
Yeah. A 78 I believe, right? Was it ever on LP? I don't remember ever seeing it.
I don't think so. No, I don't think it was ever on LP, because -- I believe Juan Tizol played the solo. I think it goes back that far.
Uh-huh.

You know? How I remembered it, I guess I was highly impressed with it after all these years. I never played it. Well, with the absence of the guys now, the things in the bottom of my memory begin to surface again, and I didn't realize how much that I'd really listened, and not playing it, you know. I didn't play it, never practiced it, nothing else, you know?

Didn't you play it -- I had heard you play it before, because that's how I knew you knew it, and I suggested to Kenny, 'Ask Jimmy Jones to play "Orson,"' but I don't know when it was I heard you do it. Was it possibly when you and John were with the group?
John Collins, yes. At Dante's.
Yeah.
And then, I'll tell you, I played it on Ellington's birthday. We had a --
Yeah, that must have been the last time I heard it, at Dante's on Ellington's birthday.
Yeah. There was Bill Berry. Let's see, Ray Brown was with us. Jake Hanna. I think Jake Hanna played. I played piano, and I can't think of who else, but I played it. And it was well received.
Oh, it was beautiful. I was so impressed, that's why I wanted to hear it again, especially on record, so
I could keep hearing it again.

Yeah. Well, I -- and I hadn't touched it, I think I touched it about two or three times, and when we were in Berkeley, I just sat down and started playing it again, you know? Nat Adderley, Cannonball's brother, said, "Well, what is that?" It was funny. I said, "Well, this is one of those hidden great things of the Ellington family," you know.
